title: Autotune defaults: batching/caching, quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Desai
description: Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost for common production workloads by providing safe, conservative defaults and automated profile recommendations for batching, KV prefix caching, and quantization. This PR implements an autotune pipeline that: (1) infers workload characteristics from traffic samples, (2) recommends batching and cache defaults, (3) attaches quantization profiles tuned for latency/cost tradeoffs, and (4) exposes a unit-economics (uecon) CLI/API for teams to validate expected cost delta before rollout. The changes are conservative by default (no forced quant changes); operators must opt into recommended quant profiles. Highlights: - Add autotune core service (pkg/autotune) that analyzes request traces and synthesizes actionable defaults. - Add runtime integrations to apply defaults as lightweight config overlays (runtime/batcher.go, runtime/kv_cache.go). - Introduce quantization profile manifests and a selection engine (model/quant/profiles). - Surface recommendations via a uecon CLI and REST endpoint (tools/uecon, api/uecon). - Add end-to-end tests and benchmarks comparing baseline vs recommended settings. Checklist: - [x] Autotune analysis proto and storage - [x] Safe default overlay application path - [x] Quant profile format + validator - [x] UEcon CLI + API + example reports - [x] Unit tests and integration canary - [x] Docs (docs/optimize/autotune.md) Related work: ENG-4321 (autotune design doc), ENG-4488 (quant profiles RFC), PM-214 (product acceptance criteria). See design: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4321/autotune-batching-caching and RFC: https://interna.redwood/eng/rfcs/quant-profiles. Rollout plan: merge to main behind feature flag (autotune.enable=false); enable for internal canary (redwood-perf) for two weeks; then publish recommendations to Console as opt-in suggestions. No forced model changes or infra migrations in this PR.
